quests.instruction: Shadow the correction. Which words carry the biggest peaks?
quests.word: I ordered the chicken, not the fish.
quests.textToSpeak: I ordered the chicken, not the fish.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈɔːdəd ðə ˈtʃɪkɪn | ˈnɒt ðə ˈfɪʃ/
quests.hint: Say the two foods as if they were opposites on a scale.
quests.explanation: The two dishes are being contrasted, so both nouns peak and everything else steps back.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: the two items being compared take the biggest peaks.

quests.instruction: Shadow the defence. Which word in the first clause sounds most prominent if the speaker means 'it wasn't me'?
quests.word: I didn't take your charger, Maya borrowed it.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't take your charger, Maya borrowed it.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈdɪdnt ˈteɪk jə ˈtʃɑːdʒə | ˈmaɪə ˈbɒrəʊd ɪt/
quests.hint: Imagine pointing at yourself while you say it.
quests.explanation: Stressing 'I' tells the listener that someone else did it, which 'Maya' then confirms.
quests.flowRule: Focus on the Subject: stress the person who is being ruled out.

quests.instruction: Shadow the choice. Why do 'this' and 'that' stand out more than 'one'?
quests.word: Which one did you want, this one or that one?
quests.textToSpeak: Which one did you want, this one or that one?
options: They are the contrasting words, so 'one' stays light
They are the longest words in the two phrases
They come first in each phrase, so they get the beats
quests.correctAnswer: They are the contrasting words, so 'one' stays light
quests.ipa: /ˈwɪtʃ ˈwʌn dɪdʒə ˈwɒnt | ˈðɪs ˈwʌn ɔː ˈðæt ˈwʌn/
quests.hint: Compare what changes between the two phrases.
quests.explanation: The difference between the options is 'this' and 'that', so those take the peaks.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: the word that changes between parallel phrases is stressed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the clarification. Which ideas get the strongest stress?
quests.word: I said she's coming on Thursday, not that she's already here.
quests.textToSpeak: I said she's coming on Thursday, not that she's already here.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈsed ʃiz ˈkʌmɪŋ ɒn ˈθɜːzdeɪ | ˈnɒt ðət ʃiz ɔːlˈredi ˈhɪə/
quests.hint: Think about future arrival versus arrival that has happened.
quests.explanation: The two ideas differ in time of arrival, so 'coming' and 'already here' carry the contrast.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: opposite ideas receive the peaks.

quests.instruction: Shadow the reframing. What does the stress pattern do?
quests.word: It's not a problem, it's an opportunity.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not a problem, it's an opportunity.
options: It treats both nouns as unimportant
quests.ipa: /ɪts ˈnɒt ə ˈprɒbləm | ɪts ən ˌɒpəˈtjuːnəti/
quests.hint: Say the two nouns with a bit of extra energy.
quests.explanation: The reframe works because the two nouns are placed on matching peaks.
quests.flowRule: Parallel Contrast: matching stress highlights the replaced word.

quests.instruction: Shadow the careful defence. Which words carry the contrast?
quests.word: I didn't say she was rude, I said she was direct.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't say she was rude, I said she was direct.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈdɪdnt ˈseɪ ʃi wəz ˈruːd | aɪ ˈsed ʃi wəz dɪˈrekt/
quests.hint: Notice which words are not repeated.
quests.explanation: The speaker repeats the frame and swaps only the adjective, which takes the stress.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: the swapped word is the focus.

quests.instruction: Shadow the correction. What is the effect of stressing 'six'?
quests.word: We're meeting at six, not seven.
quests.textToSpeak: We're meeting at six, not seven.
options: It shows the speaker is angry
quests.ipa: /wɪə ˈmiːtɪŋ ət ˈsɪks | ˈnɒt ˈsevn/
quests.hint: Imagine someone just said 'seven'.
quests.explanation: Stressing the number corrects an earlier wrong assumption.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: stress the corrected item.

quests.instruction: Shadow the pushback. Which word takes the peak in the last clause?
quests.word: Who said I was upset? I'm not upset, I'm tired.
quests.textToSpeak: Who said I was upset? I'm not upset, I'm tired.
quests.ipa: /ˈhuː ˈsed aɪ wəz ʌpˈset | aɪm ˈnɒt ʌpˈset | aɪm ˈtaɪəd/
quests.hint: Think about which word replaces the wrong guess.
quests.explanation: 'Tired' replaces 'upset', so it takes the peak.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: the replacement word is stressed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the instruction. Why does 'that' stand out?
quests.word: Not that file, the other one on the desktop.
quests.textToSpeak: Not that file, the other one on the desktop.
options: It is a new topic that the speaker introduces
It is the last word, so it takes the final peak
It rules out one specific file
quests.correctAnswer: It rules out one specific file
quests.ipa: /ˈnɒt ˈðæt ˈfaɪl | ði ˈʌðə ˈwʌn ɒn ðə ˈdesktɒp/
quests.hint: Imagine someone picking the wrong file.
quests.explanation: 'That' points at the wrong file, so it gets a peak before the correction.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: demonstratives take the peak when rejecting a choice.

quests.instruction: Shadow the defence of a colleague. Which words contrast?
quests.word: He's not lazy, he's exhausted.
quests.textToSpeak: He's not lazy, he's exhausted.
quests.ipa: /hiz ˈnɒt ˈleɪzi | hiz ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd/
quests.hint: Look for a swap of explanation.
quests.explanation: The speaker replaces a negative label with the real reason.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: replacing a label.

quests.instruction: Shadow the retort. Which words are stressed?
quests.word: I wasn't talking to you, I was talking to Dan.
quests.textToSpeak: I wasn't talking to you, I was talking to Dan.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈwɒznt ˈtɔːkɪŋ tə ˈjuː | aɪ wəz ˈtɔːkɪŋ tə ˈdæn/
quests.hint: The verb repeats; the person changes.
quests.explanation: The repeated verb is weak; the audience changes.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: the changed element is stressed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the careful pushback. Which words take the heaviest stress?
quests.word: I'm not saying you're wrong, I'm saying the timing is risky.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not saying you're wrong, I'm saying the timing is risky.
quests.ipa: /aɪm ˈnɒt ˈseɪɪŋ jɔː ˈrɒŋ | aɪm ˈseɪɪŋ ðə ˈtaɪmɪŋ ɪz ˈrɪski/
quests.hint: The verb repeats; look for what the speaker actually wants to challenge.
quests.explanation: 'Wrong' is the idea being rejected and 'timing' is what the speaker is really questioning.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: reject one idea and replace it, with both on a peak.

quests.instruction: Shadow the accusation. Which pair of words carries the escalation?
quests.word: He didn't just forget, he ignored it completely.
quests.textToSpeak: He didn't just forget, he ignored it completely.
quests.ipa: /hi ˈdɪdnt dʒəst fəˈɡet | hi ɪɡˈnɔːd ɪt kəmˈpliːtli/
quests.hint: Imagine the speaker raising the seriousness in the second clause.
quests.explanation: 'Forget' is the milder claim and 'ignored' is the stronger one, so both receive a peak.
quests.flowRule: Escalating Contrast: the word that replaces a weaker claim is stressed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the complaint. Why is 'I' strong in the second clause?
quests.word: Everyone else got a bonus, but I didn't.
quests.textToSpeak: Everyone else got a bonus, but I didn't.
options: It is the last word, so it takes the final peak
It starts a clause, so it gets the main stress
quests.ipa: /ˈevriwʌn ˈels ˈɡɒt ə ˈbəʊnəs | bət ˈaɪ ˈdɪdnt/
quests.hint: Say it as if you were excluded.
quests.explanation: 'I' stands against 'everyone else', so it takes a peak and 'didn't' follows lightly.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: pronouns can take a peak when they are the exception.

quests.instruction: Shadow the assessment. Which two nouns take the peaks?
quests.word: She's got the experience, but not the confidence.
quests.textToSpeak: She's got the experience, but not the confidence.
options: 'got' and 'not', the verb and the negative
quests.ipa: /ʃiz ɡɒt ði ɪkˈspɪəriəns | bət ˈnɒt ðə ˈkɒnfɪdəns/
quests.hint: Which two qualities are being compared?
quests.explanation: The speaker evaluates two qualities, so they take parallel stresses.
quests.flowRule: Parallel Contrast: contrasted qualities take parallel stress.

quests.instruction: Shadow the careful clarification. Which verbs carry the contrast?
quests.word: What I said was we'd consider it, not that we'd do it.
quests.textToSpeak: What I said was we'd consider it, not that we'd do it.
quests.ipa: /ˈwɒt aɪ ˈsed wəz wiːd kənˈsɪdər ɪt | ˈnɒt ðət wiːd ˈduː ɪt/
quests.hint: Look at what the speaker promised versus what they did not.
quests.explanation: The promise is only to consider, so 'consider' and 'do' take the peaks.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: verbs can carry the contrast when the action is disputed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the defence. Why is 'cheap' repeated with a peak?
quests.word: I know it's cheap, but cheap isn't the same as bad.
quests.textToSpeak: I know it's cheap, but cheap isn't the same as bad.
options: It introduces a new idea, so it is stressed
It is the final word, so it carries the nuclear peak
It starts a correction of an assumption
quests.correctAnswer: It starts a correction of an assumption
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈnəʊ ɪts ˈtʃiːp | bət ˈtʃiːp ˈɪznt ðə ˈseɪm əz ˈbæd/
quests.hint: The speaker is changing the meaning of 'cheap'.
quests.explanation: The repeated word is a fresh peak, because the speaker is separating two ideas.
quests.flowRule: Repeated Focus: a repeated word can take a new peak to correct an assumption.

quests.instruction: Shadow the complaint. Which verbs are stressed?
quests.word: You said you'd call me, not text me.
quests.textToSpeak: You said you'd call me, not text me.
quests.ipa: /jə ˈsed jʊd ˈkɔːl mi | ˈnɒt ˈtekst mi/
quests.hint: Notice that 'you said you'd' and 'me' repeat.
quests.explanation: Only the two actions differ, so 'call' and 'text' take the peaks and 'me' is light the second time.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: the differing actions take the peaks.

quests.instruction: Shadow the clarification. What is the focus of the speaker's question?
quests.word: No, I'm asking whether it's possible, not whether it's easy.
quests.textToSpeak: No, I'm asking whether it's possible, not whether it's easy.
quests.ipa: /ˈnəʊ | aɪm ˈɑːskɪŋ ˈweðər ɪts ˈpɒsəbl | ˈnɒt ˈweðər ɪts ˈiːzi/
quests.hint: Look at the word that changes between the two clauses.
quests.explanation: The speaker wants to know if it can be done at all, not how difficult it is.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: the stressed adjective names the real question.

quests.instruction: Shadow the explanation. Which words take the biggest peaks?
quests.word: She didn't leave because of the money, she left because of the manager.
quests.textToSpeak: She didn't leave because of the money, she left because of the manager.
quests.ipa: /ʃi ˈdɪdnt ˈliːv bɪˈkɒz əv ðə ˈmʌni | ʃi ˈleft bɪˈkɒz əv ðə ˈmænɪdʒə/
quests.hint: Both clauses share the same frame.
quests.explanation: Because the frame repeats, only 'money' and 'manager' differ and take the stress.
quests.flowRule: Frame Repetition: repeated words fade; the changed words peak.

quests.instruction: Shadow the feedback. Which word does 'only' point to?
quests.word: Only the second paragraph needs changing, the rest is fine.
quests.textToSpeak: Only the second paragraph needs changing, the rest is fine.
quests.ipa: /ˈəʊnli ðə ˈsekənd ˈpærəɡrɑːf ˈniːdz ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ | ðə ˈrest ɪz ˈfaɪn/
quests.hint: 'Only' focuses on the word that follows it.
quests.explanation: 'Only' marks the limiting focus, so 'second' takes the peak.
quests.flowRule: Focus Particles: 'only' draws the peak onto the word it limits.

quests.instruction: Shadow the clarification. Which nouns carry the contrast?
quests.word: I'd say it's more of a suggestion than a rule.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd say it's more of a suggestion than a rule.
quests.ipa: /aɪd ˈseɪ ɪts ˈmɔːr əv ə səˈdʒestʃən ðən ə ˈruːl/
quests.hint: Notice what is being compared.
quests.explanation: The two nouns are compared, so both receive peaks.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: compared nouns peak.

quests.instruction: Shadow the status update. Which words are most prominent in the second clause?
quests.word: We've tested the software, but we haven't tested the hardware.
quests.textToSpeak: We've tested the software, but we haven't tested the hardware.
quests.ipa: /wiv ˈtestɪd ðə ˈsɒftweə | bət wi ˈhævnt ˈtestɪd ðə ˈhɑːdweə/
quests.hint: The verb is repeated; the focus shifts to what is missing.
quests.explanation: The negative and the new object are the news, so they are stressed.
quests.flowRule: Frame Repetition: repeated words fade, and the negative plus the new item peak.

quests.instruction: Shadow the correction. Which words carry the stress?
quests.word: Not tomorrow, the day after tomorrow.
quests.textToSpeak: Not tomorrow, the day after tomorrow.
options: 'not' and 'the', the negative and the article
'after' and 'not', the preposition and the negative
quests.ipa: /ˈnɒt təˈmɒrəʊ | ðə ˈdeɪ ˈɑːftə təˈmɒrəʊ/
quests.hint: The second 'tomorrow' is repeated information.
quests.explanation: The wrong date is stressed, and the new date is contrasted, while the repeated 'tomorrow' is weak.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: the repeated word fades.

quests.instruction: Shadow the pointed question. Which verbs are stressed?
quests.word: Did you finish the draft or just start it?
quests.textToSpeak: Did you finish the draft or just start it?
quests.ipa: /dɪdʒə ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə ˈdrɑːft | ɔː dʒəst ˈstɑːt ɪt/
quests.hint: The question hinges on the verbs.
quests.explanation: 'Finish' and 'start' are the alternatives, so both verbs take a peak and 'draft' is weak.
quests.flowRule: Alternative Contrast: alternatives are stressed.

quests.instruction: Shadow the preference. Which words get the main beats?
quests.word: Honestly, I'd rather have a small salary and a short commute.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, I'd rather have a small salary and a short commute.
options: 'honestly' and 'rather', the opener and the modal
'have' and 'and', the auxiliary and the conjunction
quests.ipa: /ˈɒnɪstli | aɪd ˈrɑːðə hæv ə ˈsmɔːl ˈsæləri ən ə ˈʃɔːt kəˈmjuːt/
quests.hint: The two adjectives mirror each other.
quests.explanation: The pairs 'small salary' and 'short commute' are in parallel and take peaks.
quests.flowRule: Parallel Stress: matching phrases share beat patterns.

quests.instruction: Shadow the pointed correction. Which pair of words carries the meaning shift?
quests.word: It's not that she can't do it, it's that she won't.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not that she can't do it, it's that she won't.
quests.ipa: /ɪts ˈnɒt ðət ʃi ˈkɑːnt ˈduː ɪt | ɪts ðət ʃi ˈwəʊnt/
quests.hint: Notice that everything else is identical in both halves.
quests.explanation: The two halves are identical except for ability versus willingness, so only 'can't' and 'won't' peak.
quests.flowRule: Contrastive Stress: when two clauses match, the single changed word is the focus.

quests.instruction: Shadow the reminder. Which pairs mirror each other?
quests.word: I asked for the report on Monday, and for the slides on Tuesday.
quests.textToSpeak: I asked for the report on Monday, and for the slides on Tuesday.
options: 'asked' with 'asked', the repeated verb in each part
'for' with 'on', the two prepositions in the line
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈɑːskt fə ðə rɪˈpɔːt ɒn ˈmʌndeɪ | ən fə ðə ˈslaɪdz ɒn ˈtjuːzdeɪ/
quests.hint: Two items are matched to two days.
quests.explanation: Two deliverables and two days create a matched pair of peaks.
quests.flowRule: Parallel Contrast: paired items take matching peaks.

quests.instruction: Shadow the quick exchange. Where does the stress move in 'fourteen' when it corrects 'forty'?
quests.word: Did you say forty? No, fourteen.
quests.textToSpeak: Did you say forty? No, fourteen.
options: It stays on the first syllable, FOUR-
It splits evenly across both syllables
quests.ipa: /ˈdɪdʒə ˈseɪ ˈfɔːti | ˈnəʊ | ˌfɔːˈtiːn/
quests.hint: The difference between the two numbers is at the end.
quests.explanation: To separate 'fourteen' from 'forty', the speaker stresses the final syllable -teen.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Stress Shift: stress moves to the syllable that distinguishes the words.

quests.instruction: Shadow the careful defence. Which word is the main focus of the first clause?
quests.word: I never said he stole the money, I said he took it by mistake.
quests.textToSpeak: I never said he stole the money, I said he took it by mistake.
quests.ipa: /aɪ ˈnevə ˈsed hi ˈstəʊl ðə ˈmʌni | aɪ ˈsed hi ˈtʊk ɪt baɪ mɪˈsteɪk/
quests.hint: Which word is replaced by 'took it by mistake'?
quests.explanation: 'Stole' is the accusation being denied, so it takes the peak.
quests.flowRule: Corrective Focus: stress the word being rejected.
